question.text: The Ottomans conquered this capital city of the Byzantine Empire in May 1453. Give its name as of 1453, not its ancient name or its modern name, which was adopted in 1923.
question.answerHtml: Constantinople (do not accept or prompt on “Byzantium” or “Istanbul”)
question.clue: A bronze column originally from Delphi which depicted three entwined serpents holding up a golden bowl was relocated to this city's Hippodrome.

swap.text: The Byzantine Empire had several rulers with this common name; the first of whom usurped the throne from Michael III and founded the Macedonian dynasty, and the second was known as the Bulgar-slayer for his complete conquest of Bulgaria.
swap.clue: In addition to naming the brother-in-law of Vladimir I of Kiev, this name belongs to a ruler who overthrew Michael III and had Ignatius installed over Photius as patriarch of Constantinople.

question.text: This Byzantine Emperor tasked Belisarius with reconquering the Mediterranean, and this husband of Theodora was targeted in the Nika Riots.
question.clue: A work denouncing this ruler becoming wealthy off of the "sky tax" includes the hyperbole that "ten thousand times ten thousand times ten thousand" people died during his reign.

swap.text: Constantinople was earlier sacked during this campaign, which led to the decline of the Byzantine Empire. Enrico Dandolo, the Doge of Venice, had earlier led this campaign.
swap.clue: Pope Innocent III excommunicated all of its participants when they attacked the Dalmatian capital in exchange for assistance from Enrico Dandolo, the doge of Venice.

question.leadin: Name some things about the times when the use of religious images were opposed by both religious and Byzantine authority.
question.text: Name that time period during which depictions of religious figures was directly opposed by the leaders of the Eastern Church.
question.clue: The first attempt to apply this doctrine officially was met with resistance at the Chalke Gate, and it was condemned by the Second Council of Nicaea convoked by Irene.

swap.text: This man, one of Justinian's generals, helped Narses ease the Nika Riots. He also led various wars against the Vandals and Ostrogoths and was given the last ever Roman Triumph at their conclusion.
swap.clue: This general's campaigns informed Procopius's History of the Wars.

question.leadin: Before invading England, Harald Hardrada of Norway served as a mercenary in this military order.
question.text: Name this elite army unit that served as the personal bodyguards to the emperors of the Byzantine Empire.
question.clue: As punishment for replacing this group with loyal Scythians, Michael V ("the fifth") was castrated and blinded by Harald Hardrada.

swap.text: Justinian almost fled Constantinople during these riots that started after an angry crowd gathered at the Hippodrome.
swap.clue: Participants in this event wanted to crown Hypatius, but were outmaneuvered by the eunuch Narses and slaughtered by Mundus.

question.text: According to George Akropolites, Tsar Kaloyan of Bulgaria made a skull cup out of the head of a ruler with this name. This name was shared by the first Latin Emperor of Constantinople as well as the Leper King of Jerusalem.
question.clue: This cousin of Rudyard Kipling highlighted the power of aerial attacks by noting that "the bomber will always get through."

swap.text: This majestic Byzantine church, whose name means "Holy Wisdom," was designed by Anthemius of Tralles and Isidore of Miletus.
swap.clue: On its southwestern entrance of this building is a mosaic of two important emperors presenting models of this building and its city to the Virgin Mary.

question.leadin: Answer the following about innovations created by the Mongols.
question.text: After founding the Mongol Empire, Genghis Khan created one of these systems, known as the Yassa, in order to maintain order. One of these systems created by Hammurabi of Babylon was carved into a stone stele.
question.answerHtml: law codes [accept reasonable equivalents, such as legal systems; prompt on laws or codes]
question.clue: One work of this kind included sections like the Digest and the Institutes.

swap.text: This general helped put down the Nika Riots by capturing Hypatius. This Byzantine general recovered provinces of the Western Roman Empire in the Gothic War and conquered the Vandal Kingdom.
swap.clue: Early in this leader's career, together with Mundus they were instrumental in ensuring Hypatius and Pompeius did not take the throne.

question.text: The most famous member of this family temporarily ended the Great Schism with the Second Council of Lyon after reclaiming Constantinople from the Latin Empire. That man, Michael VIII, established this family as the final Byzantine dynasty.
question.clue: Michael VIII founded this dynasty, which expelled the Crusaders from Constantinople in 1261 and were the last to rule Byzantium before the Turkish conquest in 1453.

swap.leadin: Description acceptable. To accomplish this action, the men involved hid certain kinds of eggs and larvae in their bamboo canes.
swap.text: Identify this sixth-century event that was perpetrated by two Nestorian monks returning from China to Constantinople.
swap.answerHtml: smuggling silk into the Byzantine empire [accept obvious equivalents]
swap.answer: smuggling silk into the Byzantine empire

question.leadin: Name some people whose writings serve as important primary sources about the Byzantine Empire.
question.text: This woman may have been inspired by the material laid out by her husband Nikephoros Bryennios the Younger to write a chronicle of her father's rule named the Alexiad.
question.clue: This woman wrote admiringly of the manly traits of Empress Irene in her influential Byzantine history, The Alexiad.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about an uprising FTPE.
swap.text: The participants, who were named after two of the four colors worn by charioteers, rebelled against the policies of Justinian I in 532.
swap.clue: Belisarius and Narses put down this 532 riot driven by unruly factions of chariot racing fans.

question.leadin: This ruler recognized Stefan Nemanja ("NEH-mahn-yah") as the rightful zupan ("zhoo-pan") during an incredibly successful campaign through Serbia.
question.text: Identify this expansionist Byzantine emperor whose reign was chronicled by his loyal historian John Cinnamus. He magnanimously forgave Raynald of Chatillon ("shah-tee-YON") for his Cyprian massacre in exchange for total fealty.
question.clue: While this ruler's armies besieged the island of Corfu, the Venetians mocked this ruler by having an African slave impersonate him.

swap.text: This sixth-century Alexandrian traveler is sometimes known by an alternate Greek name meaning "traveler to India." This man's Christian Topography contains a map in which the universe, in the shape of the Tabernacle of Moses, contains a rectangular, flat earth.

question.leadin: Identify the following people important in the life of Justinian I, FTPE.
question.text: The primary source for information during Justinian's reign is the Secret History by this man, secretary to Belisarius.
question.clue: Perhaps the most famous Byzantine historian, this author portrayed unflattering depictions of such contemporaries as Justinian, Theodora, and Belisarius in his Secret History.

swap.leadin: One of this historian's most outlandish claims was that the ruler he served could turn his head invisible at will, which he did while walking around his palace.
swap.text: Name this historian whose more serious works include a narrative of wars against the Sassanids, Vandals, and Ostrogoths.
swap.clue: In one work, this historian describes how two slaves would scatter barley onto the genitals of a theatrical performer which geese would then remove; that performer was brought to the stage after their father Akakios, a bear keeper for the Greens, died.
